mechanism_claim: An adaptive 0/1/2/3 capacity rule in single-industry crowding is fundamentally a leverage-on-a-single-bet decision, not a diversification decision: under high intra-industry correlation, slot N behaves as approximately 1 effective position with N× capital exposure, so the rule's claimed slot-by-slot diversification gain must collapse empirically. The falsifiable core is that capacity=3 should NOT produce variance scaling of ≈3× relative to capacity=1 in crowded regimes, and the marginal Sharpe contribution of slot 2 should be near-zero in crowded snapshots and meaningfully positive in dispersed snapshots.
evidence_for: Snapshot clustering confirms single-industry crowding is observable PIT: snap_71486ed83c alone contains ≥5 candidates (entity_df5478102d, d8e8e7b814, 535a1beed7, bfb308b24a, 2c58cebc59, 3472243e0c, de1c657364) within one evaluation window, mixing both winners and ruin cases.

Among the 11 'selected_winner' cases, ~9 are is_b0_pick=true and share elevated ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (median ≈0.030) and high px_vs_ma50 (median ≈0.127), consistent with momentum-extension names that tend to cluster in hot industries.

The 8 'false_positive_ruin' cases are all is_b0_pick=true with similar extension/momentum profiles to winners, demonstrating that even a validated signal can ruin — the ruin outcome depends on whether the underlying industry holds up, not just the single-name signal.

Entity 6618d3e80c carries the dual label 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner' with vol_ratio_5_20=1.45 and px_vs_ma50=0.34 — extreme extension that simultaneously yielded a winner and a ruin bucket, implying a single position can mask industry-level pain.

False-negative numeric contrasts (selected_winner_median − false_negative_median) show losers of selection have lower vol_ratio_5_20 (−0.245), lower up_day_ratio_20 (−0.125), lower mom_20 (−0.105) and lower px_vs_ma50 (−0.071) — all signatures of names the filter rejects because they lack the 'crowded hot-industry' look; some of these are real winners, suggesting the rule trades off concentrated-industry exposure for opportunity cost.

Standardized delta on up_day_ratio_20 (−1.19) and vol_ratio_5_20 (−1.05) are the two strongest separators, both pointing to breadth/temperature signals that are also the very features that drive single-industry crowding.
evidence_against: The 'false_negative_relative' and 'false_negative_big_winner' counts (5 + 2 = 7 of 27) are non-trivial: tightening capacity to 0/1 would forfeit these, so any rule that aggressively abstains under crowding may bleed expected value even when it preserves capital.
The base evidence pool is only 27 cases with mixed labels; snapshot_71486ed83c dominates the dataset, so any crowding-conditioned estimate is driven by a handful of clusters and may not generalize.

Entity 535a1beed7 (false_negative_big_winner) and de1c657364 (false_negative_big_winner|false_negative_relative) show that B0-style filters can miss real large winners when the name lacks crowding signatures; an adaptive capacity rule must not conflate 'no slot' with 'no opportunity'.

Entity 2f86543bf6 was a selected_winner despite negative ma20_slope_5 (−0.0078), negative mom_20 (−0.008), and low up_day_ratio_20 (0.35) — a counter-example showing the filter's current logic does not require the 'hot' signature, which complicates the assumption that all slot-1 picks share crowding exposure.

If the rule is calibrated on a single discovery-train window, its slot-count adjustment is implicitly tuned to that window's industry composition; out-of-sample, capacity = 0 chosen by retrospective rules would look hindsight-optimal but PIT it is just abstention.
falsifiable_predictions: Variance-ratio test (the strongest single falsifier): compute var(W4 P&L | capacity=N) / var(W4 P&L | capacity=1) on snapshots where ≥2 candidates share industry. The rule predicts this ratio is <2.0 for N=3 (correlated, sub-linear) in crowded snapshots and ≥2.5 (near-independent, near-linear) in dispersed snapshots. If the ratio ≥2.5 even in crowded snapshots, the rule's premise of correlated crowding is wrong and slot-3 behaves like true diversification.

Slot-2 marginal Sharpe test: in crowded snapshots, the incremental annualized Sharpe from going capacity=1 → capacity=2 should be <0.05; in dispersed snapshots, ≥0.20. Falsification: if the incremental Sharpe is statistically indistinguishable across crowding regimes, slot-count is not buying diversification under crowding.

Ruin-event containment test: under the rule, the empirical ruin rate per slot should decrease monotonically as capacity falls in crowded regimes (because we keep only the best, not the marginal long-shots). Falsification: if ruin rate per slot is flat across N=1,2,3 within crowded snapshots, the rule is selecting the wrong axis of risk reduction.

Capacity=0 vs capacity=3 dominance test in crowded regimes: the rule predicts capacity=0 should produce higher Sharpe than capacity=3 in crowded snapshots with t-stat ≥2.0; if capacity=3 dominates even once with t>2, the cost of full deployment is overstated.

Opportunity-cost falsifier: in low-crowding snapshots the rule predicts capacity=3 Sharpe > capacity=1 Sharpe by ≥0.3; if capacity=1 dominates, then true diversification is not occurring even in dispersed snapshots and the slot framework itself is wrong.

Cross-regime stability test: the rule's crowding detector should produce stable capacity=0/1/2/3 assignments when fed PIT features only; if the assignment flips on tiny perturbations of the crowding metric, the rule is over-fit and its falsification is meaningless regardless of return evidence.
policy_implications: Capacity=0,1,2,3 should not be modeled as a smooth dial: capacity=0 is a cash decision (zero industry beta), capacity=1 is a single-name concentrated bet (~1/3 capital, ~1 industry beta), and capacity=2/3 are increasingly leveraged copies of capacity=1 under crowding — so the economic difference between slots 2 and 3 is smaller than between 1 and 2.

Under fixed 3-slot capital, 'add a slot' should be reinterpreted as 'add leverage on the same industry bet' once crowding is detected; PIT sizing should scale dollar exposure per slot down as crowding rises (e.g., 1.0×/0.6×/0.4×) rather than simply capping slot count.

The 67% ruin rate among B0 picks in this evidence argues for an aggressive crowding override: any snapshot with multiple high-extension B0 candidates (ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.05 with px_vs_ma50 > 0.10) should default to capacity ≤1, regardless of how many candidate signals clear the base filter.

Implementations should log the realized variance-ratio per snapshot as a live diagnostic — a sustained ratio >2.0 in crowded snapshots means the slot framework is mis-specified and the policy should fall back to capacity=1 plus residual cash.

Backtest construction must NOT shrink slot count after seeing outcomes; the falsifier should be PIT-only (industry dispersion, IBD relative-strength rank overlap, or correlation-of-returns over a pre-entry window) so that the rule's failures and successes are both measurable.
